newsitem.title: USA: First-time jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: First-time jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up to collect unemployment benefits for the first time fell last week, the government reported Thursday.
The Labour Department said 8,000 fewer people applied for jobless benefits in the week ended April 19, bringing the number of claims down to 324,000 from an unrevised 332,000 in the previous week.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 328,000 for the week ended April 19.

The four-week moving average of claims -- viewed by economists as a more accurate indicator of jobless trends -- rose in the same week. It stood at 323,000 in the week ended April 19, up from 319,750 the prior week.
The four-week moving average for the week ended April 19 was the highest since Feb. 8 week, when it reached 325,500, the department said.
The total number of Americans continuing to collect jobless benefits fell by 4,000 to 2.29 million in the week ended April 12, the latest period for which that data were available.
The department said 10 states and one territory reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended April 12, the latest period for which that data were available.
Among the largest were Michigan with 4,200, Puerto Rico with 2,767, North Carolina with 2,746, Alabama with 2,566, Washington with 2,055 and Pennsylvania with 2,002.

Michigan reported layoffs in the automobile industry, while Puerto Rico said it had layoffs in the apparel, leather goods and petroleum industries. North Carolina reported layoffs in the textile, furniture and transportation equipment industries.

Alabama had layoffs in the textile, apparel, trade and service industries. Pennsylvania attributed the increase to layoffs in the fabricated metals and service industries. Washington provided no reason for the increase in claims.
There were six states reporting decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the April 12 week.
They were California with 3,275, New Jersey with 2,547, Oregon with 1,948, Illinois with 1,750, Massachusetts with 1,558 and Arkansas with 1,080.
New Jersey said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries and Illinois reported fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and manufacturing.
California and Oregon gave no reason for the drop in claims while Arkansas said it had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment industries.
